title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide
author: Alicia Chen
body:
Summary

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's people operations guidelines for hiring, candidate experience, new-employee onboarding, the performance and feedback cycle, and manager responsibilities. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, and new managers. The procedures below reflect our commitment to scalable, equitable hiring and a consistent employee experience across hosted, dedicated, and private teams.

Scope

- Applies to all full-time employees, contractors on long-term engagements (>3 months), and interns where noted.
- Includes interview process design, offer & negotiation, preboarding, first-day and 90-day onboarding, continuous feedback, and annual performance cycles.

Key Principles

- Candidate-first: Transparent timelines, clear expectations, timely communication (48-hour cadence for scheduling and 5 business days for offers).
- Structured assessment: Use consistent rubrics and role-specific scorecards to reduce bias and improve calibration.
- Manager-led onboarding: Hiring managers own role-level onboarding; people-ops supports platform-level onboarding.
- Continuous feedback: Frequent, lightweight check-ins combined with formal reviews twice per year (mid-year and year-end).

1) Hiring process (standardized, inclusive)

Quick reference timeline (target):
1. Requisition approval: 3-7 business days (manager + finance + hiring committee)
2. Sourcing & screening: 1-4 weeks depending on role seniority
3. Interview loop: 1-2 weeks
4. Decision & offer: 48-72 hours after final debrief

Interview loop template (engineering example)
- Recruiter screen (30 min): role fit, basic compensation expectations, must-have skills
- Technical screen (45-60 min): coding/system design or take-home depending on level
- Onsite loop (remote/in-person, 3-4 interviews, each 45-60 min):
  - Problem-solving (team engineer) - rubric: correctness, approach, communication
  - System design / architecture (senior roles) - rubric: tradeoffs, scalability, clarity
  - Product sense / cross-functional collaboration (PM partner) - rubric: tradeoffs, stakeholder influence
  - Culture & hireability interview (hiring manager) - rubric: learning orientation, ownership, communication

Scoring and decision
- Use the role-specific scorecard in Lever (or GitHub HR plugin) with a 1-5 scale across competency areas.
- Hiring manager collects scores and synthesizes decision. A passing candidate typically has majority "3" or higher and no critical "1" in safety/security or collaboration.
- All decisions must include a written summary (1-3 paragraphs) capturing strengths, risks, and recommended leveling.

Diversity & inclusion requirements
- Diverse slate requirement: For senior and above roles, include at least two external candidates from underrepresented groups or two different sourcing channels before moving to onsite.
- Interviewer diversity: Prefer at least one interviewer from outside the immediate team.

Offer & negotiation
- Offers are approved by manager + finance + people-ops. Use the compensation bands document for target ranges.
- Offer letters include base salary, equity grant range, target bonus, target start date, and basic benefits summary. Require candidate acceptance or counter within 7 calendar days.

2) Preboarding & First Day (operational checklist)

Preboarding (owner: people-ops + IT + hiring manager):
- Send welcome packet within 48 hours of offer acceptance: start date, orientation agenda, point of contact, Slack ID, and required paperwork links.
- Create accounts (email, SSO, Okta), hardware request submitted to IT, and repo access requests filed 5 business days before start where possible.
- Assign buddy (peer) and schedule 1:1s for week 1.

First day agenda (sample):
- 09:00-09:30: Welcome + people-ops orientation (benefits, payroll, policies)
- 09:30-10:30: Team intro + manager 1:1 (role expectations)
- 10:30-12:00: System access walk-through + local dev environment setup
- 13:00-17:00: Orientation training modules and first small task assignment

Onboarding 30/60/90 day plan (manager-owned template)
- 0-30 days: Complete orientation, meet cross-functional partners, deliver small onboarding task, and review success criteria.
- 31-60 days: Begin contributing to team goals, own a small deliverable, and present findings/suggestions to the team.
- 61-90 days: Full ownership of a project or feature, calibration with manager on role expectations, and completion of 90-day review.

Table: Minimum access & completion checkpoints
| Checkpoint | Owner | Target date | Completion evidence |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Email & SSO access | IT | Day 0 | Success login screenshot |
| Code repo access | Team eng lead | Day 1 | PR created or cloned repo |
| Security training | Security | Day 7 | Training completion cert |
| Manager 30/60/90 review scheduled | Manager | Day 7 | Calendar invites present |

3) Performance & feedback cycles

Cadence
- Informal feedback: Continuous. Encourage weekly 1:1s and immediate feedback for important events.
- Formal reviews: Mid-year and year-end for all employees. Calibration weeks follow each formal review to align leveling and compensation recommendations.

Review components
- Self-assessment (employee): Strengths, areas to improve, key contributions, and career goals.
- Manager assessment: Role competencies, examples, overall rating (scale: Exceeds / Meets / Needs Improvement), development plan.
- Peer feedback: Collected anonymously for cross-functional signals.
- Calibration: Group review led by people-ops to normalize ratings across teams.

Rating guidance (short):
- Exceeds expectations: Routinely delivers beyond scope, enables others, demonstrates significant impact.
- Meets expectations: Consistently delivers on role responsibilities with expected impact.
- Needs improvement: Gaps in performance or collaboration requiring measurable improvement plan.

Performance improvement plans (PIP)
- Trigger: Two consecutive "Needs Improvement" ratings or a critical incident as defined by manager + people-ops.
- Process: 30-90 day written plan with objectives, success metrics, weekly manager check-ins, and HR oversight.
- Outcomes: Successful completion (return to normal cycle), extension with revised objectives, role change, or separation.

4) Manager responsibilities (practical checklist)

Hiring
- Define role with clear success criteria and leveling, partner with recruiter to craft job description, review and sign off on scorecards.
- Attend calibration and hiring committee interviews.

Onboarding & ramp
- Provide a clear 30/60/90 plan, schedule necessary access and training, meet weekly for the first 12 weeks, and collect early feedback.

Feedback & development
- Conduct weekly 1:1s and document outcomes in shared notes.
- Prepare thoughtful written feedback for formal reviews and contribute to peer feedback.
- Own development conversations, propose stretch assignments, and manage career laddering discussions.

Risk & escalation
- If an employee is at risk (performance or behavior), notify people-ops within 5 business days and follow the investigation/triage checklist in the incident response policy.

5) Templates & examples (links and copyable text)

- Offer checklist (copyable): Role, level, base, equity, bonus, start date, hiring manager, recruiter, finance approver, people-ops approver.
- 30/60/90 template (copyable): Goals, success criteria, milestones, stakeholders, learning plan.
- Manager 1:1 agenda template: Progress updates, blockers, career discussion, action items.

6) Training, enablement, and resources

- Mandatory trainings: Security basics, privacy/data handling, and anti-harassment completed within first 2 weeks.
- Manager enablement: Quarterly manager training covering interviewing, feedback calibration, and mental health support resources.
- People-ops office hours: Weekly drop-in for hiring & onboarding questions.

7) Metrics & reporting (how we measure success)

- Time-to-fill (target): 30 days for IC roles, 60 days for senior hires.
- Offer acceptance rate (target): >= 70% overall; >= 60% for senior roles.
- New hire retention (90-day): target >= 95% active.
- New hire ramp (qualitative): Manager-rated "meets expectations" at 90 days for >= 80% of hires.

Appendices

A. Interviewer code of conduct
- Be punctual, prepared, and respectful. Provide actionable feedback and avoid questions about protected characteristics.

B. Confidentiality & data handling
- Candidate data is stored in Lever and only shared on a need-to-know basis. Follow the Security & Compliance page for retention periods and access controls.

C. Frequently asked questions
- Who schedules security training? IT & Security teams coordinate and people-ops tracks completion.
- Who does the 90-day review? Hiring manager, with input from the buddy and cross-functional leads.

Owner & escalation
- Document owner: People Ops (Alicia Chen). For escalations or suggested updates, contact people-ops@redwood-inference.com.

Change history
- 2024-10-15: Created (initial consolidation).
- 2025-06-01: Added diverse slate policy and updated offer acceptance targets.
- 2026-02-20: Updated review cadence and clarified PIP timelines.

End of document
